segments.say: Lesson 24. Design: Enterprise Knowledge Assistant. Full A I system-design round: "Design a chatbot over 2M internal docs for 50k employees, with permissions."

A full A I system-design round: design a company-wide assistant that answers questions from millions of internal documents, respects permissions, and stays accurate, fast and affordable. Here is an analogy. Designing a smart company librarian: a back office that keeps the catalogue up to date, a front desk that answers fast, and strict rules about who may read which files.

Why does this matter? This is the most likely A I design question for GenAI/rag roles. It ties together everything in the rag and evals segments. A few key words. Functional requirements: What it must do (answer with citations). Non-functional requirements: How well (latency, scale, security). A C L: Access control list: who can see a document. Ingestion pipeline: Background process that indexes documents.

High-level architecture. Requirements first. Functional: Q&A with citations, follow-ups, permission-aware. Non-functional: p95 under 5 s to first useful output, 50k users, ~2M docs, fresh within 1 hour, no data leaks.

Back of envelope: 2M docs times ~10 chunks equals 20M chunks times 1024 dims times 4 B about 80 G B of vectors (H N S W: more). 50k users times 5 Q/day about 250k Q/day about 3 Q P S on average, ~30 at peak.
Async ingestion: connectors emit change events to a queue, workers parse, chunk, embed and attach A C L metadata (groups allowed), and upsert into a hybrid index. Deletes and updates propagate too.
User authenticates via S S O. The A P I resolves their groups. The Lang Graph orchestrator condenses the follow-up into a standalone query.
Hybrid retrieval with an A C L pre-filter (only chunks the user can see), then reranking. Permission filtering must happen at retrieval, never after generation.
Generation through the gateway (routing, caching, failover). Thread state is persisted for follow-ups. Stream the answer with citations.
Trace everything. Offline evals (context recall, faithfulness) gate releases, plus online judges and thumbs feedback. Dashboards for latency, cost and "I don't know" rate.

Scale: stateless A P I pods, sharded vector index with replicas, caches. Trade-offs to discuss: freshness versus ingest cost, reranker latency versus quality, managed versus self-hosted models (data residency).

The A I system-design answer framework. Clarify users, use cases, scale, latency, accuracy bar, data sensitivity. Estimate docs, chunks, vector storage, Q P S, tokens/day leads to cost. High-level design with ingestion and query paths drawn separately. Deep dives: chunking, retrieval, A C Ls, prompting, agent loop. Evaluation & observability. Interviewers love this; most candidates skip it. Safety, scale, cost, failure modes and trade-offs.

Deep-dive talking points. Permissions: A C L metadata on every chunk, pre-filtered at query time. Sync group changes. Test cross-tenant leakage in evals. Freshness: change-data-capture or webhooks leads to queue leads to incremental re-embed. Tombstone deletes. Tables & attachments: special parsers, table-to-text, multimodal captions. "I don't know": thresholds on reranker scores, then refuse rather than guess. Cost: 250k Q/day times ~4k tokens about 1B tokens/day, so routing and caching matter.
Red flags interviewers watch for. Jumping to "use G P T-4 plus Pinecone" without requirements. Filtering permissions after the L L M sees the docs. No evaluation plan. No mention of cost.

Say it in the interview. "I separate an async ingestion pipeline (connectors leads to queue leads to workers that chunk, embed and tag A C Ls leads to hybrid index) from a real-time query path (S S O leads to orchestrator leads to permission-filtered hybrid retrieval leads to rerank leads to gateway-routed generation with streaming citations). Quality is gated by offline rag evals and monitored with online evaluators, and I size the vector store and token spend up front.".

Key decisions & trade-offs. Vector store: pgvector (simple), managed / sharded (Pinecone, Qdrant), B at 20M+ chunks. Permissions: post-filter results, pre-filter in index, pre-filter (no leaks). Freshness: nightly batch, event-driven incremental, event-driven. Model: single frontier, router: small plus frontier, router. Orchestration: L C E L chain, Lang Graph agent, Lang Graph if follow-ups/tools.

A likely interview question: Design a rag assistant over internal docs, in 60 seconds. A strong answer: Clarify scale, latency and permissions. Async ingestion: connectors leads to queue leads to parse/chunk/embed with A C L tags leads to hybrid index. Query: S S O leads to orchestrator condenses query leads to A C L-filtered hybrid retrieval leads to rerank leads to routed L L M with streaming citations. Evals gate releases, tracing and online judges in prod, caching and routing for cost.
That's it for Design: Enterprise Knowledge Assistant. Now play the quiz and games in the app to lock it in. See you in the next lesson.
